newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Morocco issues T-bond at 8.5-9.5 pct on bourse.
newsitem.headline: Morocco issues T-bond at 8.5-9.5 pct on bourse.

text.p: Morocco's finance ministry announced on Monday a discounted public T-bond issue on the Casablanca bourse at between 8.5 and 9.5 percent interest rate.
"We issued today on the Casablanca bourse a discounted public Treasury bonds at between 8.5 and 9.5 percent interest rate aimed at stimulating the bond market," a ministry spokesman told Reuters.
Subscription will be closed on March 28, 1997, the spokesman said.

The Treasury bonds called "Emprunt National" are listed on the stock exchange as part of the state domestic debt oriented to small investors and will be negotiable on the market from March 31, 1997, an analyst at Casablanca Finance Intermediation said.

"The government bonds shows interest rates down 0.5 percent...The bonds were issued as follows: one-year bond at 8.5 percent, three-year bond at 9.0 percent and five-year bond at 9.5 percent," the analyst said.
Earlier this month, Morocco's monetary authorities decided to cut by half a point (0.50 percent) interest rates on short and medium public Treasury bond issues.
The bonds divided in tranches of 5,000 dirhams ($532) and 50,000 dirhams ($5,319) are open to the public and all operators including foreign institutions, a bourse official said.

In the past, institutional investors were barred from access to public treasury bond issues, including insurance companies. But since September 1996, institutional investors have been allowed to subscribe to these bonds, the official said.
The government issues public T-bonds every three months and it was the second time it cut interest rates by 0.50 percent in a period of six months, he added.
The government move coincided with Morocco's commercial banks decision to cut interest rates by two points on medium and long term investment loans to small and medium-sized firms, a banker said.

The Casablanca-based GPBM bankers' association earlier said the rate reduction decision was effective from March 1 to December 31, 1997 "to contribute significantly to the country's economic relaunch."
King Hassan urged banks and the finance ministry, in his throne speech on March 3, to cut interest rates on loans particularly to small and medium-sized firms.
Total domestic borrowing more than doubled in 1995 to 13 billion dirhams from 5.2 billion dirhams in 1994, Bank al-Maghrib central bank said in its latest report.
A Casablanca-based stockbroker estimates at 19 billion dirhams the total amount of the Treasury bonds issues in 1996.
